title: Human–AI search improves high-degree Mahler-measure constructions
summary: A Gemini-assisted search and symbolic-analysis loop produced polynomial constructions that improve six previously published Mahler-measure records. The source verifies irreducibility symbolically and evaluates measures numerically. This advances particular constructions; it does not resolve Lehmer’s conjecture or establish global optimality at every degree.
ai_technology: Internal Gemini versions including Gemini 4 Argon, coupled to Google Antigravity
organization: Google DeepMind; California Institute of Technology

evidence.tested: Reported record improvements at degrees 178, 188, 190, 202, 242 and 250; broader construction evaluated through degree 2,000.
evidence.unknown: Search is not exhaustive and does not prove global minima. Irreducibility checks use Mathematica, while Mahler measures use numerical roots; we did not reproduce either. Self-consistent cyclotomic-free construction is distinct from a universal irreducibility proof.
evidence.ai_role: Gemini co-developed search and verification tools and collaborated with researchers to convert numerical patterns into a five-parameter construction.

source_review.scope: Primary v1 agent workflow, search verification, construction, provenance and discussion; current v1 history. No independent computational reproduction.
